clue.text: In part, is trusting model employer?

indicators.note: 'In' tells the solver the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, spanning the word breaks

parts.note: the letters run across the end of part, all of is and the start of trusting

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone who trusts people is a good boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model employer' reads as an ideal boss, but it means someone who hires a model to sit for them.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter or sculptor pays a sitter to pose, so they literally employ models.

clue.text: Formal meeting for people in house

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an official interview, as with a monarch or pope
second meaning: the spectators filling a theatre

explanation.surface: A formal meeting arranged for the members of a parliamentary house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' suggests parliament, but it is the theatre auditorium, as in a full house.
explanation.definitionFit: One is granted an audience with royalty, and a theatre's paying crowd is also its audience.

clue.text: Old craft of European pursuing unusual métier

indicators.note: to pursue is to come after, so the European piece is placed behind the other
something unusual is out of its normal form, so the word beside it has its letters rearranged

parts.note: the word as printed, but the parse needs an R where it has its second E: the setter's slip
E is the standard abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A European who has taken up an odd old craft or trade.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter slipped: métier rearranged cannot give the needed letters, as it has an E where an R is wanted. 'Craft' means a vessel, not a skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme was an ancient Greek or Roman warship with three banks of oars.

clue.text: Modern pirate runs after sailor within island

indicators.note: 'after' sets the runs abbreviation behind the rest
'within' places the sailor inside the island's name

parts.note: Skye is an island of the Scottish Hebrides
jack, or jack tar, is an old word for a sailor
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A sailor on an island who goes running, perhaps in a pirate tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The sailor sits inside the island, giving SKYJACKE, and the runs letter goes on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A skyjacker hijacks an aircraft, which is piracy of the air, a modern version of seizing ships.

clue.text: Mike, Charlie, Oscar, and Victor appear in it on radio

definitions.text: Mike, Charlie, Oscar, and Victor appear in it on radio

parts.words: Mike, Charlie, Oscar, and Victor appear in it on radio
parts.note: surface reading: four men are cast members in some radio drama
setter's reading: these are code words for the letters M, C, O and V used in radio communication

explanation.surface: Four named actors share billing in a radio show.
explanation.walkthrough: The names are entries in the NATO phonetic system, where each letter has a code word for clear radio speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The NATO phonetic list assigns a word to every letter, so those names stand for letters within it.

clue.text: It's bound to be available for a few people

definitions.text: It's bound to be available for a few people

parts.words: It's bound to be available for a few people
parts.note: surface reading: something that is certain to be on offer only to a small group
setter's reading: bound as in a book with a binding, printed in small numbers

explanation.surface: Something guaranteed to be on offer to only a select few.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' reads as 'certain to', but it means a book that has been bound.
explanation.definitionFit: A book printed in a restricted number of copies is a rare run that only a few buyers can own.

clue.text: In coastal resort, left poor accommodation

indicators.note: 'In' places the left abbreviation inside the resort's name

parts.note: Hove is a seaside town beside Brighton on England's south coast
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone left behind in a seaside town with only shabby lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter goes inside at the very end of the resort's name, so the result simply appends it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hovel is a small squalid dwelling, the poorest kind of housing.

clue.text: String player in Beethoven's first needing help

indicators.note: 'first' takes only the opening letter of the composer's name

parts.note: the opening letter of the composer's name
to assist is to help

explanation.surface: A string player struggling with Beethoven's First Symphony needs some help.
explanation.walkthrough: Beethoven's First sounds like the symphony, but it is just his initial.
explanation.definitionFit: A bassist plays the double bass or bass guitar, both instruments with strings.

clue.text: Coaches in one part of speech or another

parts.words: Coaches in one part of speech or another
parts.note: surface reading: someone tutors pupils in grammar, one word class or another

parts.words: one part of speech or another
parts.note: setter's reading: the answer is a verb meaning coaches, and as a noun it means sets of railway coaches

explanation.surface: A tutor coaches students on one grammatical word class or another.
explanation.walkthrough: Take 'coaches' as a verb and the answer is a synonym; take it as a noun and the answer is what the carriages make up.
explanation.definitionFit: To coach is to instruct, a synonym as a verb; as a noun, linked railway carriages form a locomotive-drawn set.

clue.text: As result of fighting, there's nothing in life a cruel war ruined

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of shape, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, is nothing
the words themselves as fodder

explanation.surface: A grim reflection that a brutal war leaves nothing in life intact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fighting' fits the war picture, but it means boxing or wrestling.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeated blows to the ear cause swollen, lumpy cartilage, a common injury among boxers and rugby forwards.

clue.text: Host returning, having traversed distant part of country

indicators.note: to traverse is to stretch across, so the reversed host spans around the distant word
returning means going back, so the word for host is read from end to start

parts.note: a host is a great number, a myriad
far means distant

explanation.surface: A host comes back from a trip across a remote region of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' looks like someone entertaining guests, but here it is a multitude. 'Country' means the countryside, not a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A dairy farm is a piece of rural land given over to milk production, a portion of the countryside.

clue.text: Through crossing street, what's seen down avenue

indicators.note: crossing means lying across, so the first word spans around the street abbreviation

parts.note: via means by way of, through
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Directions for the view you get walking through a junction down a street.
explanation.walkthrough: The street words all seem part of the picture, but only one is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A vista is a long narrow view, especially one framed by trees or buildings along a road.

clue.text: Where pupil is placed, subject to examination

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the organ that holds the pupil, the dark opening of the eye
second meaning: a verb, to stare at closely

explanation.surface: A school pupil is seated where exams are held.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pupil' and 'examination' suggest school, but the pupil belongs to the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The pupil is part of the eye's globe, and to inspect something closely is, informally, to stare hard at it.

clue.text: Not like unusually well-read Oxford professor

indicators.note: unusually means not in the ordinary way, so the letters are set in a new arrangement

parts.note: the words themselves as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone unlike the typical bookish Oxford academic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well-read' suggests erudition, but it means widely read by the public.
explanation.definitionFit: J R R Tolkien was a professor of Anglo-Saxon at Oxford whose novels have huge readerships.

clue.text: Rebuff queen may deliver, but never king

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a repulse or setback that halts something

definitions.text: queen may deliver, but never king
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the chess attack on a king, which any piece but a king can give

explanation.surface: A royal snub that a queen hands out but a king never would.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess a king can never attack the opposing king, since it may not move next to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A check is a stopping or restraint, and in chess it is a threat to capture the enemy king.

clue.text: Accuracy in copying not shown by cheater

definitions.meaning: first meaning: faithfulness of a reproduction
second meaning: faithfulness in a relationship, which an unfaithful partner lacks

explanation.surface: An exam cheater who copies accurately without being spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copying' and 'cheater' suggest an exam, but the cheater is an unfaithful partner.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means faithfulness, both of a reproduction to its original and of a partner to a spouse.

clue.text: Fish or fruit only

parts.note: a lemon is a citrus fruit
sole means only, as in sole survivor

explanation.surface: A shopper choosing between fish and fruit and nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or' sounds like a choice, but it only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon sole is a European flatfish of the plaice family, widely eaten.

clue.text: Contributor to person's descent or ascent, possibly

definitions.text: Contributor to person's descent or ascent, possibly

parts.words: Contributor to person's descent or ascent, possibly
parts.note: surface reading: someone helping a climber go down or up a mountain
setter's reading: descent means lineage, and ascent recalls the evolutionary Ascent of Man

explanation.surface: A helper aiding a mountaineer's climb or descent.
explanation.walkthrough: Darwin's 'Descent of Man' and Bronowski's 'Ascent of Man' both describe human lineage, hence 'possibly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear is one from whom a person is descended, so is part of their family line.

clue.text: Exaggerated merits of old solver, wrecked by end of crossword

indicators.note: 'end of' picks the last letter of crossword to add to the mix

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old

indicators.note: something wrecked is broken up, so the letters gathered here are rearranged

parts.note: the word itself as fodder
the final letter of crossword

explanation.surface: An old solver hyped up the merits of a crossword that then defeated him.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversell something is to praise its qualities beyond what they deserve.

clue.text: Produce some rhyming slang, initially kept in check

indicators.note: 'kept in' means held inside, so that letter goes inside the word for check

parts.note: to verify is to check

indicators.note: 'initially' takes only the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of slang

explanation.surface: Someone composes Cockney rhyming slang while keeping themselves restrained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rhyming slang' is a phrase in the surface, but the definition ends at 'rhyming'.
explanation.definitionFit: To versify is to put into verse, writing lines that rhyme.

clue.text: Chap embracing openings provided by secret organization?

definitions.text: Chap embracing openings provided by secret organization?

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the chap's word goes around those letters

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: openings are starts, so the first letters of the following two words are taken

parts.note: the first letters of secret and organization

explanation.surface: A man accepts the opportunities a secretive society offers him.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a man taken into a secretive fraternity. The question mark flags the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Freemason belongs to a fraternal society famous for its secret rituals and signs.

clue.text: Relative is upset over superficially attractive stuff

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word is read bottom to top
in a down clue 'over' puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: the word is, turned round
bling is showy, flashy jewellery

explanation.surface: A family member gets cross about someone's flashy taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads as an emotion, but it turns the little word over.
explanation.definitionFit: A sibling is a brother or sister, a close family member.

clue.text: Without reason, brought up request for material

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means raised from bottom to top, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: someone mad has lost their reason
to ask is to request

explanation.surface: A demand for cloth raised unreasonably.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a reversible patterned fabric, originally silk from Damascus.

clue.text: Article by poet laureate cut short? Just so

definitions.text: Article by poet laureate cut short? Just so

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the poet's name drops its final letter

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
Robert Bridges was Britain's Poet Laureate from 1913 to 1930

explanation.surface: A writer asks whether a laureate's article was trimmed, and is told yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just so' confirms the wordplay is also the meaning: the answer is a verb meaning cut short, and the name is itself cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten it, condensing it while keeping its sense.

clue.text: Wild animal seen in feeding orgy and covered in gore

definitions.text: Wild animal seen in feeding orgy and covered in gore

indicators.note: 'seen in' says the letters are visible inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters span the end of feeding and the start of orgy

explanation.surface: A predator spotted at a blood-soaked feast on a carcass.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue paints the animal at a kill, while the hidden letters sit across the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: The dingo is Australia's wild dog, a pack hunter that tears into its prey.

clue.text: With half of score accomplished, it's okay to defend

parts.note: a score is twenty, half of which is ten
able means skilled, accomplished

explanation.surface: A sports team that has already scored half its points thinks it can sit back.
explanation.walkthrough: A score is the old English word for twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenable position or argument is one that can be held or maintained against attack.

clue.text: Like the majority of people, wrong about answer after answer

indicators.note: 'after' places that whole piece behind a second answer letter

parts.note: A is the standard abbreviation for answer

indicators.note: 'about' means surrounding, so the wrong word goes around a letter

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
A again for answer

explanation.surface: Most people get it wrong, answer after answer.
explanation.walkthrough: The second answer letter sits inside the wrong, and that comes after the first one.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia holds well over half the world's population, so most humans are from that continent.

clue.text: Record one's temperature, following author and environmental expert

indicators.note: 'following' puts the author's name before the rest, since the rest follows it

parts.note: Umberto Eco was the Italian author of The Name of the Rose
to log is to record
one is I, so one's becomes I'S
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A green campaigner takes their temperature after the writer does.
explanation.walkthrough: Roman numeral one is I, and the apostrophe-s is kept as an S.
explanation.definitionFit: An ecologist studies how organisms relate to their surroundings, an expert on the natural world.

clue.text: Where all the pieces of poetry you write are in a row

definitions.text: Where all the pieces of poetry you write are in a row

parts.words: Where all the pieces of poetry you write are in a row
parts.note: surface reading: a place where a poet's works are lined up, as on a shelf
setter's reading: every letter of those three words lies along the top line of the typing layout

explanation.surface: A shelf where every poem you have composed is lined up.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'poetry', 'you' and 'write' are all found in the top row QWERTYUIOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A typing board lays out letter keys in rows, and the top row holds every letter of those words.

clue.text: Some work secured by the writer with right business deal

indicators.note: 'with' adds the right abbreviation alongside
to be secured by something is to be held fast by it, so the work unit sits inside the writer

parts.note: the writer of a clue refers to themselves as me
the erg is a small unit of work in physics
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A writer secures some work and gets the right business agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A merger is the combining of two companies into one, a type of corporate transaction.
